data.content_ref: inline:The target proposes a causal mechanism (fragmentation error causes checklist panel failure in non-linear tasks) but frames its refutation condition around whether a checklist can be structured as a non-linear graph capturing gestalt patterns. This is a category mismatch: the proposed relation is causal dependence (fragmentation error → failure), but the refutation targets representation capability rather than the causal claim. A checklist being representable as a non-linear graph does not refute that fragmentation error causes failure in the original linear checklist panels — it merely shows an alternative structuring exists. The refutation-if condition is misaligned with the relation it claims to neggate.
